metadata.description: Single-plugin marketplace exposing the cc-enforcer discipline plugin.

plugins.name: cc-enforcer
plugins.description: Rules your coding agent physically cannot ignore. A Claude Code plugin (and LLM-agnostic rule pack) that stops reactive patching, guessed citations, surface-level fixes and premature "done" claims by intercepting the agent's own tool calls rather than asking it nicely. PreToolUse denies an edit before it lands — editing a file you never opened this session, a suppression marker with no adjacent why-comment, a hardcoded secret or user-home path, the fourth small patch to one file, a dangerous shell flag. A nine-layer Stop gate then refuses to let a completion claim end the turn without evidence, a convergence self-quiz, a fidelity check against the user's ORIGINAL request, and a one-line TL;DR. Twelve rules, eight backed by a hook; "Imperial Edict" regexes you define per project; a repo-wide sync gate; CI drift gates that derive every documented number from the code so the documentation cannot rot. Zero dependencies, stdlib only, Linux + Windows CI, and every guard fails OPEN — a bug in the discipline can never brick your agent. v0.36.0 adds a demo you can run yourself: the same task, twice, against identical starting files, with the hooks as the only variable. `charge()` raises KeyError when the payment gateway declines — loud, immediate, pointing straight at the line that caused it. WITHOUT the plugin all five reactive edits land: the crash is swallowed into a `None`, the suite turns red, and a sign-off claiming it is green ends the turn with nothing checking the claim. WITH the plugin three of the five are refused — the `try/except: pass`, the fourth small patch to the same file, and the evidence-free completion claim — and the run is pushed into one systematic rewrite that names the root cause (the gateway has two response shapes and the old body knew only one). The subject is the LAGGING error: patching a loud failure does not remove it, it makes it quiet. A stack trace becomes a ledger holding rows the gateway never accepted, and nothing reports it until someone reconciles a statement weeks later. Both transcripts render to terminal SVGs embedded in both READMEs, replacing the hand-drawn 'before' mock-ups they used to carry. Every cc-enforcer verdict in the images is verbatim hook stdout, every test and probe result is captured from a real run, and the agent's five moves are scripted — stated plainly, because a demo that overstated itself would be the exact defect this plugin exists to catch. tests/test_demo.py re-runs the demo and compares against the committed images byte for byte, so a change to any hook's wording fails CI instead of leaving a stale picture on the front page; and because that equality check alone would be satisfied by a demo that had stopped denying anything, it also asserts each of the three verdicts by content and asserts the unguarded run still ends in a silent failure. 682 -> 690 tests, then 691 in v0.36.1, which fixed the demo images: they were rendered on Windows, so the deny banner carried a backslash-joined path that Linux reproduces with a forward slash, and a byte-for-byte pinned artefact may not contain a platform-dependent string. Fixed at the mechanism and asserted by its own test. Prior — v0.35.2 registers a fourth co-update group in this repo's own sync gate: editing any `hooks/scripts/*_guard.py` now requires a README sweep in the same session, or an explicit sync-check line saying why none is needed. The group was asserted by the user, not inferred by the scanner — a heuristically guessed co-update invariant is fabricated confidence, and the whole value of the gate is that a human said these files move together. Writing it then produced a fresh instance of the very class it closes: v0.35.1's new checks made three behavioural claim classes derivable, while the gate's own design notes still declared prose behaviour and citation accuracy uncoverable wholesale — a doc describing its own tool as weaker than it is. `test_doc_sync`'s docstring, `tests/README.md` and `docs/README.md` were swept in one change, and the note now separates the derivable sub-classes (a sentence naming a pattern, an arithmetic result, or an identifier) from the judgement prose that genuinely is not checkable. 682 tests, unchanged. Prior — v0.35.1 is a documentation-truth release. The active half of rule 12 — the repo-refresh full-repo scan, unrun since v0.32.2 — found that both READMEs advertised a detector that does not exist: the layer-(b) row named "should be fine" and "应该" as hedges, the before/after demo was built on "Should be stable now", and the sample output claimed `Hedge matched: 'Should be'`. Bare `should` is deliberately excluded from the hedge set, as stop_guard's own comment states, so the demo's OUTPUT could not have come from its own INPUT — a plugin whose whole purpose is refusing unfounded claims was making one on its front page. v0.34.1 had aligned the injected PROMPTS down to the implementation and scoped that sweep to prompts/; the READMEs describe the same detector and were never in the sweep, so the class was closed on one surface and left open on another. Two siblings: the rolling-patch sample printed a per-file coverage bar of "1104 of 3672 chars" where lib/editscale computes 1102 (numbers a reader would take for captured output, written by hand), and docs/ARCHITECTURE.md's Stop decision table cited HEDGED_DONE_REASON, NO_EVIDENCE_REASON, MISSING_QUIZ_REASON and MISSING_FIDELITY_REASON — four identifiers deleted in v0.12.0 and cited for the twenty-three releases since. Correcting the words would decay on the next release, so each class got a gate: hedge trigger examples derived from stop_guard._HEDGE_INNER, sample coverage bars from editscale.coverage_bar, and every backticked UPPER_SNAKE identifier in a non-CHANGELOG doc must resolve to a real definition or be registered as a doc-only exception with a reason. All three were verified RED against the pre-fix tree first, because a gate that only passes on fixed content cannot tell a working check from a deleted one. Two candidate findings were retracted during the same scan rather than shipped: a marketplace "mojibake" that was the terminal's cp936 rendering, and an AKIA "false negative" that was the documented placeholder hatch firing on a value containing EXAMPLE. This description was also trimmed from 18,496 characters: it had accumulated nine stacked release narratives duplicating CHANGELOG.md — the same second-source defect CLAUDE.md §6.1 diagnosed and fixed for itself. 676 -> 682 tests. Full release history: CHANGELOG.md.
